title: Data Leakage
description: The parent user may unintentionally share sensitive information (email, password, name, govt ID) during registration, leading to potential data leakage if the information is intercepted or misused.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store sensitive user data (email, password, name, govt ID) insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access or breaches.

title: Data Misuse
description: The authentication service may misuse the collected data (email, password, name, govt ID) for purposes other than intended, such as marketing or profiling without user consent.

title: Unintended Disclosure
description: There is a risk that the authentication service may unintentionally disclose sensitive user information to unauthorized parties due to misconfigurations or vulnerabilities.

title: Data Disclosure from Authentication Service
description: The authentication service may inadvertently disclose personal data when storing parent account information in the MongoDB users collection, especially if the data includes sensitive information that is not strictly necessary for the operation.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB
description: The MongoDB users collection may expose personal data to unauthorized access or breaches, leading to potential data disclosure of parent account information stored within it.

title: Data Leakage
description: The authentication service may inadvertently expose sensitive user data (JWT + user data) to unauthorized parties during the transmission process.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The parent user may mishandle the received JWT and user data, leading to potential exposure or misuse of sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse
description: The parent user may use the received JWT and user data for purposes other than intended, leading to privacy violations.

title: Legitimate User Data Exposure
description: The child user may inadvertently expose their parent’s email and password during the login process, especially if the device is shared or compromised.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store the parent’s email and password insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access.

title: Data Misuse by Service
description: The authentication service may misuse the parent’s email and password for purposes other than authentication, such as marketing or profiling.

title: Data Leakage
description: The authentication service may inadvertently expose sensitive child profile information when generating JWTs, especially if the JWT is not properly secured or if the service is misconfigured.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The child user may mishandle the received JWT or child profile data, leading to unauthorized access or exposure of sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse
description: The child user may use the received data inappropriately, such as sharing it with unauthorized parties or using it for unintended purposes.

title: Linking of Child Profile Data
description: The act of sharing child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) by the Parent User may lead to linking threats, where the combination of these attributes could be used to identify the child or associate them with other data, potentially revealing sensitive information.

title: Inadequate Access Control on Child Profile Data
description: Once the child profile data is created and stored in the Child Profile Management process, inadequate access controls may lead to unauthorized access or misuse of the data by internal or external parties.

title: Data Retention and Deletion Issues
description: The Child Profile Management process may not have proper data retention and deletion policies, leading to the potential for unnecessary storage of sensitive child data, increasing the risk of data breaches or misuse.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profile Management
description: The process of storing or updating child profiles may lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data, either explicitly or implicitly, especially if the data shared is more than what is necessary for the operation.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB Child Profiles Collection
description: The MongoDB child profiles collection may inadvertently expose personal data to unauthorized access or third parties, leading to potential data disclosure risks.

title: Data Leakage through User Actions
description: Child User may unintentionally share personal data (e.g., location, preferences) while searching, liking, or commenting on videos, leading to potential data leakage.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not adequately manage personal data collected from Child Users, leading to non-compliance with data protection regulations.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The metadata associated with video files may contain identifiable information, which can lead to privacy concerns if not properly managed.

title: Data Disclosure of Personal Data
description: There is a risk of personal data being disclosed when video metadata and files are stored and retrieved from the MongoDB collection, potentially exposing sensitive information.

title: Data Disclosure of Child Profiles
description: The process of storing child search and watch history may lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data if proper access controls are not implemented. This could result in sensitive information being exposed to unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure from MongoDB Collection
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may inadvertently disclose personal data if security measures are insufficient, allowing unauthorized access to stored child profiles and their associated search and watch history.

title: Lack of User Consent
description: The parent user may upload videos without providing explicit consent for the processing of their personal data, leading to a lack of legal basis for data processing.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not manage personal data properly, leading to potential non-compliance with data protection regulations.

title: Lack of consent for data sharing
description: The video management service may stream videos to the child user without obtaining proper consent, leading to a lack of legal compliance and potential privacy violations.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The child user may not manage their personal data properly after receiving the video, leading to potential misuse or exposure of sensitive information.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profiles
description: The child browsing data stored in the MongoDB childprofiles collection may be disclosed to the AI Recommendation Engine, potentially leading to the exposure of personal data without proper consent or necessity.

title: Inadequate Data Handling by AI Engine
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may inadequately handle the child browsing data, leading to unintended inferences or misuse of personal data.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4) is sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers (External Entity EE3), which may include personal data. This transfer of data can lead to explicit or implicit disclosures of personal information, violating the minimality principle by potentially sharing more data than necessary for advertising purposes.

title: Data Disclosure by Third-Party Advertisers
description: Once the browsing data is received by third-party advertisers (External Entity EE3), there is a risk that they may use or share this data in ways that lead to further disclosures of personal information, either intentionally or unintentionally. This could include using the data for targeted advertising without proper consent or safeguards.

title: Data Disclosure of Government ID Images
description: The authentication service (Process) may unintentionally disclose government ID images during the storage process, either through explicit sharing with unauthorized parties or through implicit means such as metadata exposure.

title: Data Disclosure of Stored Government ID Images
description: The file system (DataStore) may expose stored government ID images to unauthorized access, leading to potential data breaches or misuse of sensitive personal information.

title: Linkability Threat
description: The act of storing JWT in localStorage can lead to linkability threats if the JWT contains identifiable information that can be linked to a user’s actions across different sessions or applications.

title: Inaccessibility Threat
description: If the JWT stored in localStorage is not properly secured, it may be accessible to unauthorized scripts or browser extensions, leading to potential information leakage.

title: Data Disclosure Threat
description: The JWT stored in localStorage may be exposed to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to retrieve sensitive information from the token.

title: Linking of Child Data to Parent
description: The process of retrieving child history for parent review may lead to linking the child's data with the parent's identity, potentially exposing sensitive information about the child.

title: Inadequate Identity Verification
description: The parent user may not be adequately verified before accessing the child's profile, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse by Parent User
description: Once the child history is retrieved, the parent user may misuse the data for purposes not intended by the system, such as sharing it with unauthorized parties.
